actions.name: Endorse a statement in two rounds (FROST-shaped scaffold)
actions.partialBecause: The registry: it exercises the multi-round seam; its own header says it is a coordination scaffold, not production FROST; superseded by btc.frost-bip445 and lez.frost-public-account.
actions.summary: A statement endorsed in two rounds, k of the room's members in each. It has FROST's shape — two rounds over a named roster — and none of its cryptography: no nonce commitments, no Schnorr aggregation, one Ed25519 signature per member per round.

steps.does: Room → + → Statement → Endorse with FROST → text → Propose. The hosted driver is the room's current members with k = min(2, members) per round. The proposal publishes its policy, the effect, and the signing context: environment 'room', account = the room's topic, slot = the intent id, expiry = now + MUSTER_INTENT_TTL_S (7 days by default). The intent id is content-addressed from the effect and the policy.

Signs the materialization dCBOR ['muster.frost.v1', 'muster.effect.statement.v1', {text}] with Ed25519. The live path tags the contribution with the round the intent is collecting (1); the fold keeps one contribution per (member, round) and folds every round-1 contribution before any round-2 one. At k the core advances to round 2 — from describe().rounds, never a constant. The card shows 'round 1 of 2'.
steps.signs: an Ed25519 signature by the member's room identity (their encryption identity's Ed25519 key, held in the keystore) over the materialization: the dCBOR array ['muster.frost.v1', schema id, {field: value…}] (CDE map order, shortest integers); plus a muster attestation by the same key over P = (context, the materialization, the provenance record)

steps.does: The same act again, tagged round 2: the same Ed25519 signature over the same bytes — acceptance is round-agnostic by design (the scaffold's header). At k distinct members in round 2 the intent is executable.
steps.signs: the same Ed25519 signature over the same materialization as round 1

steps.does: Executable is the end. coordinate_submit on it answers 'not-onchain': a room family has no settlement, and the card reads '✓ Endorsed — a signed group decision. Nothing settles on-chain.'

refusals.why: no roster key verifies it; it never counts
the fold keeps one contribution per (member, round): a single member can never complete a k ≥ 2 intent
invariant 1: the conformance check refuses a materialization of another effect

refusals.what: a contribution published under a name that is not its signer's
refusals.why: it is nobody's approval: the fold and every view drop it before dedup, so one signer never counts twice and a forgery never takes a member's slot (exo-a5a)

actions.ui: Room → + → Statement → Endorse with FROST → text → Propose; the card shows 'round R of 2'; Approve once per round.

claims.claim: Both rounds must reach k before the intent is executable; the round count comes from the driver's describe()
This is not FROST: no nonce commitments, no partial signatures, no aggregate — a round-1 signature is valid in round 2

unverified: Ed25519 is deterministic and both rounds sign the same bytes, so a member's round-2 contribution equals their round-1 one; anyone in the room holding it could publish it tagged round 2 and it would count, graded unattested. From reading drivers/frost.nim and coordination/intents.nim; no test covers it.
frost is not one of the live probes' policies (probes/live_room.nim: safe, threshold), so its expiry and provenance refusals on the hosted path are not tested for this kind.
